name: Community — MiniMax H3 (Turbo LoRA, larryvrh)
author: larryvrh
description: MiniMax H3 text-to-video with the v4-600 EMA Turbo LoRA + matching dual-schedule sampler from larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora — the default choice for 6-8 steps and for any motion that is not heavy/fast, while keeping audio in sync. The current best line improves static/small-motion detail and resolves the v1 over-sharpened plastic look. Training continues, and audio plus fast-motion behaviour remain open areas, so treat this as a preview. Same base MiniMax H3 checkpoint/text-encoder/VAE as SimpliGen's official MiniMax H3 pack, so no extra large downloads beyond the ~744MB LoRA. v1.4.0 adds two image-to-video cards and changes nothing about the original three: MiniMax H3 Image to Video (Turbo, Comfy Kitchen attention) is the existing Turbo I2V recipe with ComfyUI's built-in Comfy Kitchen attention backend (about 25% faster on a 12 GB 4070 Ti, same look), and MiniMax H3 Image to Video (lightx2v 4-step) swaps in lightx2v's FL2V Turbo v1.1 LoRA at 4 steps for about 40% faster sampling at a small cost in fine detail.

presets.name: MiniMax H3 Text to Video (Turbo)
presets.description:
Describe a scene and get video with matching stereo sound in 6 to 8 steps. This is the default Turbo choice, best for static shots and small movement, and for any motion that isn't heavy or fast. It has better fine detail than the first version, without that version's over-sharpened plastic look.

Training continues, and audio and fast motion are still open areas, so treat the output as a preview.

Do not also pick this LoRA in the LoRA slot. The card applies minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors itself, and selecting it again doubles its strength, which gives over-sharp grain and artifacts. It shows up in the picker because the app lists every LoRA on disk.

Model format: int8 ConvRot.
presets.tagline: MiniMax H3 T2V with v4-600 EMA in 6-8 steps

extensions.name: ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo
extensions.description: Turbo LoRA loader node + dual-schedule sampler node (required - the workflow will fail to load without it)

requirements.notes: Same base weights as SimpliGen's official MiniMax H3 pack (pruned int8 diffusion model + NVFP4 text encoder) plus a ~744MB v4-600 EMA Turbo LoRA. Requires the ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo custom node (LoRA loader + dual-schedule sampler) - install before use. The current best line is intended for 6-8 steps and improves static/small-motion detail; training continues, with audio and fast-motion behaviour still open areas. Treat this as a preview. RAM requirement verified downward: every preset in this pack has been run repeatedly on a 32GB machine (31.2GB usable) with a 12GB RTX 4070 Ti, so the earlier 48GB figure was too conservative. The engine streams model weights rather than holding them resident, which is what makes a ~20GB checkpoint workable well under its own size. 16GB has not been tested.

presets.name: MiniMax H3 Reference to Video (Turbo)
presets.description:
Carry a character and a look into a new scene with sound, in 6 to 8 steps. Add up to nine references. This is the default Turbo choice for normal movement, with better detail on static shots and small motion.

Training continues, and audio and heavy or fast motion are still open areas, so treat the output as a preview.

Known issue: a reference video fails on every Turbo LoRA card, with the error 'The size of tensor a (3) must match the size of tensor b (2)'. Reference images and reference audio are fine, so remove the video and the job completes. For reference video, use the Community MiniMax H3 (Sol-Attn + EasyCache) R2V card, which has no Turbo LoRA. The fault is in an upstream node, not this pack.

Do not also pick this LoRA in the LoRA slot. The card applies minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors itself, and selecting it again doubles its strength, which gives over-sharp grain and artifacts. It shows up in the picker because the app lists every LoRA on disk.

Model format: int8 ConvRot.
presets.tagline: Reference images/video + v4-600 EMA in 6-8 steps

presets.name: MiniMax H3 Image to Video (Turbo, Comfy Kitchen attention)
presets.description:
The same as MiniMax H3 Image to Video (Turbo), about 25% faster, with no visible change to the picture or the sound. A five-second 960x544 shot took about 1.5 minutes against about 2 minutes on a 12 GB card, at 6 steps.

Your image becomes the first frame. Add a last frame and the model animates from one to the other.

The speed comes from ComfyUI's Comfy Kitchen attention, which is built into this card. That means it has no SageAttention, Sol-Attn or Spectrum option: stacking attention patches is what produces black renders.

Do not also pick the Turbo LoRA in the LoRA slot. The card applies it itself, and selecting it again doubles its strength.

Model format: int8 ConvRot.
presets.tagline: The Turbo I2V card with ComfyUI's Comfy Kitchen attention - about 25% faster, same look

extensions.description: Turbo LoRA loader node + dual-schedule sampler node (required - the workflow will fail to load without it)

requirements.notes: Same base weights as SimpliGen's official MiniMax H3 pack (pruned int8 diffusion model + NVFP4 text encoder) plus a ~744MB v4-600 EMA Turbo LoRA. Requires the ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo custom node (LoRA loader + dual-schedule sampler) - install before use. The current best line is intended for 6-8 steps and improves static/small-motion detail; training continues, with audio and fast-motion behaviour still open areas. Treat this as a preview. RAM requirement verified downward: every preset in this pack has been run repeatedly on a 32GB machine (31.2GB usable) with a 12GB RTX 4070 Ti, so the earlier 48GB figure was too conservative. The engine streams model weights rather than holding them resident, which is what makes a ~20GB checkpoint workable well under its own size. 16GB has not been tested. This card additionally bakes ComfyUI's Comfy Kitchen attention backend into the graph (core node, no extra install); measured about 25% faster wall time on a 12 GB RTX 4070 Ti with unchanged output. 5 s at 960x544, 6 steps, same first frame, seed and prompt: 87 s against 117 s wall time for the plain card, about 9.3 against 14.2 s per step on the same test with a 4-step LoRA. Needs engine ComfyUI v0.34.0 or newer for the attention node.

presets.name: MiniMax H3 Image to Video (lightx2v 4-step)
presets.description:
The fast image-to-video card, in 4 steps. Your image becomes the first frame. Add a last frame and the model animates from one to the other.

Against the larryvrh Turbo card, a five-second 960x544 shot took about 75 seconds instead of about 100 on a 12 GB card. The face held through a full head turn, and a sung line came through word for word with the mouth closing after it. The trade: the larryvrh 6-step card is a little crisper on skin and hair. Pick this one for speed and that one for detail.

Works at 768p and also at the 480p to 672p tiers.

The first and last frames are centre-cropped to the output aspect, so match the aspect to your picture or the head goes first.

Do not also pick the lightx2v LoRA in the LoRA slot: the card applies it itself, and selecting it again doubles its strength. Do not stack another speed LoRA (larryvrh, PDD) on top.

Model format: int8 ConvRot.
presets.tagline: MiniMax H3 I2V in 4 steps with lightx2v v1.1 - the fast card

video.displayModel: MiniMax H3 (pruned int8) + lightx2v Turbo 4-step v1.1

requirements.notes: Same base weights as SimpliGen's official MiniMax H3 pack (pruned int8 diffusion model + NVFP4 text encoder) plus lightx2v's 1.96 GB FL2V Turbo 4-step v1.1 (768p) LoRA from huggingface.co/lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo (not gated). No custom nodes beyond the user-LoRA slot. The attention backend is fixed to Comfy Kitchen inside the workflow, so this card declares no SageAttention / Sol-Attn / Spectrum support - it does not need them at 4 steps and stacking attention patches is what produces black renders. Measured on a 12 GB RTX 4070 Ti with 32 GB RAM; 16 GB RAM not tested. Same first frame, seed and prompt as the larryvrh Turbo card, 5 s at 960x544: sampling 39 s against 68 s, about 75 s against 100 s wall time. Runs at video/audio sigma shift 6/3. The LoRA was trained at 1344x768. Needs engine v0.34.0 or newer for the attention node.
